Inspect a fixed block-model partition

block_state.Rd

Build and inspect a fixed block-model partition and score it with the microcanonical stochastic block model description length of graph-tool 3.9. See minimize_blockmodel_dl to fit a partition.

Usage

block_state(graph, blocks = NULL, degree_corrected = TRUE)
block_membership(state)
block_sizes(state)
block_edge_counts(state)
block_log_likelihood(state)
block_description_length(state, degree_prior = NULL)

Arguments

graph

A graph created by graph_create().

blocks

One positive integer group label per vertex; defaults to a single group.

degree_corrected

Whether to use the degree-corrected likelihood.

state

A state created by block_state().

degree_prior

Degree-sequence prior, either "distributed" or "uniform". For block_description_length(), NULL uses the prior associated with the state.

Details

Matrix rows and columns correspond to the sorted nonempty labels. Directed counts are source by target. For undirected graphs the matrix is symmetric, and diagonal values count each within-group edge twice, including self-loops. Parallel edges and self-loops are included. The likelihood is the log probability of the observed multigraph conditional on the block counts, partition, and, for degree correction, degree sequence. It does not include priors or description length. block_description_length() adds the partition, edge-count, and, for degree-corrected states, degree-sequence priors, matching graph-tool's BlockState.entropy() with its default arguments (dense = FALSE, multigraph = TRUE, exact = TRUE). The partition prior includes the uniform prior on the number of groups, \(\log N\).

The distributed degree prior needs the number of integer partitions \(q(m, n)\). As in graph-tool, exact values are tabulated up to \(\min(\max(2E, 100), 10000)\) and an asymptotic approximation is used above that. The exact table needs about \(4 n^2\) bytes, so this package caps it at getOption("rgraphtool.q_cache_max", 5000) (about 100 MB); raise the option to 10000 for exact agreement with graph-tool whenever a group's degree sum lies between 5000 and 10000. The table is kept for the session.

States are snapshots: later graph changes do not change their statistics. If the graph has grown since the state was created, the description length is computed from the stored snapshot in R (exact partition counts, limited to 10 million table entries) instead of the native code.

Value

block_state() returns a block state. block_membership() returns vertex labels, block_sizes() returns counts by label, block_edge_counts() returns the affinity matrix, and block_log_likelihood() returns a numeric scalar in nats. block_description_length() returns the description length in nats.

See also

minimize_blockmodel_dl

Examples

g <- graph_create(3, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)))
state <- block_state(g, c(1, 1, 2))
block_edge_counts(state)
#>   1 2
#> 1 2 1
#> 2 1 0
block_log_likelihood(state)
#> [1] -0.4054651
block_description_length(state)
#> [1] 6.473891
